Almost all indicators are in the negative — and more from Ubisoft’s report
Published by
admin
Tags:
Ubisoft
Ubisoft
reported
the results of the first half of its current fiscal year (April-September 2026). The results were far from the best.
Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced
Let’s start with the losses. As Ubisoft reported, it closed the half-year with operating losses of 189.2 million euros, which is 57% higher than the previous year. Meanwhile, consolidated net losses increased by 54% to 248.6 million euros.
At the same time, Ubisoft’s revenue grew slightly. Over the half-year, the French company earned 673.6 million euros, an increase of 2.4%.
The volume of net bookings (deferred revenue) decreased by 16.5% to 644.7 million euros, of which 85% or 548.2 million euros came from digital game sales.
The largest market for Ubisoft remained North America, accounting for 45% of bookings. By platform, the breakdown was as follows: 48% from consoles, 30% from PC, and 14% from mobile.
By the end of the half-year, Ubisoft had acquired 88 million unique users for its console and PC games, while the monthly active user (MAU) count was 34 million. Both metrics were approximately at the same level as in April-September 2025.
The new operational model dividing Ubisoft teams into ‘Creative Houses’ is now fully implemented, although there are minor deviations from the original plan. The company decided to merge ‘Creative Houses’ No. 3 and No. 5 under the leadership of one executive, Julien Bares, to create a “synergistic effect.” To recap, ‘Creative House’ No. 3 develops games like For Honor, Skull & Bones, Brawlhalla, and The Crew, while ‘Creative House’ No. 5 focuses on casual and family games.
Ubisoft confirmed the launch of the Motherbrain AI division, rumors about which appeared in October. Additionally, the company opened a separate division responsible for gaming brands not assigned to any ‘Creative House.’ This division will also explore how to use new technologies to make game gameplay more innovative.
As of September 30, 2026, Ubisoft employed 15,500 people — 1,100 fewer than at the end of March 2026, and 5,200 fewer than at the end of September 2022.
